mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of the triggered instances despite the signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in > 70% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP growth by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a reduction in economic demand, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies report lower earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in > 60% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between GDPC1 drops and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production by more than 2% over the last two months indicates a strong supply-side response, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in > 40% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of housing starts (above 2000 thousand units) indicates strong demand, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing market is a leading indicator of economic health.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in > 50% of the instances when HOUST is above 2000, or if the correlation between high HOUST levels and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises & PAYEMS falls in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in > 60% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS changes on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a combination of a high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) and a low consumer price index (CPIAUCSL < 195) indicates a potential deflationary environment, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in > 60% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and low CPIAUCSL on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where a decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month during a period of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 200) indicates a demand shock, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in > 60% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of RSAFS drops and high CPIAUCSL on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
